Article 16 of Regulation (EU) 2015/757 has MRV verifiers accredited by a national accreditation body under Regulation (EC) No 765/2008, and Article 7(1) of that Regulation requires a body seeking accreditation to apply to the national accreditation body of the Member State where it is established, or to the one that Member State has had recourse to. You may go to another country's body only where your Member State has no national accreditation body and has not had recourse to another's, where those bodies do not accredit the activities you seek accreditation for, or where they have not successfully undergone peer evaluation for those activities.

cases.question: We want to become an accredited MRV verifier. What does the national accreditation body actually do to assess us?
cases.answer: It sends an assessment team that must at least do three things. Under Article 50(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/2917 the team reviews the documents and records you supply under Article 49, makes an on-site visit to review a representative sample of your internal verification documentation and assess how your quality management system and verification procedures are implemented, and witnesses a representative number of your staff assessing monitoring plans and verifying reports. Under Article 48 it is checking that you and your personnel have the competence to do this work, are in fact doing it in accordance with the Regulation, and meet the verifier requirements in Articles 37 to 45, including impartiality and independence. The team reports its findings and any non-conformities to you, you must take corrective action and respond within the time the accreditation body sets, and the body may ask for further action or carry out a follow-up assessment (Article 50(3) to (7)).

cases.question: How can I check whether the verifier we're about to hire is actually accredited for EU MRV?
cases.answer: Look it up in the accreditation bodies' public databases. Article 70(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/2917 requires each national accreditation body to set up and manage a publicly available database giving, for each verifier it has accredited, its name, accreditation number and business address, the date accreditation was granted and its expiry date, and any administrative measures imposed on it. Under Article 70(3) the body recognised under Article 14 of Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 facilitates and harmonises access to these national databases and may merge them into a single central one.

cases.question: The consultancy that drafted our MRV monitoring plan has a sister company offering verification. Can we use them as our verifier?
cases.answer: No. Under Article 45(4) of Regulation (EU) 2023/2917, drafting the monitoring plan is a consulting service that creates an unacceptable risk to impartiality or a conflict of interest when the verifier or any part of the same legal entity provides it. Article 45(5) extends this to a company that received such consulting from a consultancy having relations with the verifier that threaten its impartiality, which is considered compromised where the relations rest on common ownership, governance or management, shared resources, common finances, contracts or marketing, or common payment of commission for referring clients. Article 45(3) forbids a verifier from verifying a company that poses an unacceptable risk to its impartiality or where it has a conflict of interest.

cases.question: We run a feeder between Rotterdam and Bergen. Does the Norwegian port count like an EU port for the ETS, so the full voyage is covered, or is it only 50%?
Where do we actually buy EU allowances for our ships? Is there an exchange or auction we can go to directly?
On a Rotterdam to New York voyage only half the emissions count for the ETS. Can we allocate all the biofuel we burned to that half?
Is there an official EU standard ETS clause we can drop into our time charter parties?
Where in THETIS-MRV do I upload the revised monitoring plan? Is there an online form, or do I upload a file in a set format?
Does a voyage from Nuuk in Greenland to Copenhagen count as a voyage between two EU ports for MRV, or as an incoming voyage from outside?
